attribution.note: Zitron says this himself as the interviewer, in his own words. He is not quoting Stoller.

semantics.note: Reading 'people' as the Valley fits the context ('what I've talked about with the Valley'), and 'grown powerful' fairly restates 'grown big'. It is a firm causal claim, though made loosely in conversation.

contract.note: Reading the claim as fear being a material, not sole, cause is an ordinary and fair reading of 'because'. The speaker named no measure of power, no population and no start date. Whether keeping power at reinstatement counts as growth is left to interpretation.

evidence.note: Toner, a party to the dispute, says staff feared retaliation and found it hard to oppose his return. This is a disputed allegation. It is partial support, covering only retaining power in Nov 2023, not his broader rise.
OpenAI's own statement of board confidence after the review. It neither shows nor disproves fear of Altman.

Published 2026-04, before the evaluation date. It alleges a threat of reputational attack on Murati, which Altman does not recall, and also cites money, peer pressure and fear for the company's survival. It does not isolate fear's role in his rise.

reviews.rationale: The packet backs a narrow, disputed allegation: some OpenAI staff feared retaliation when he was reinstated in Nov 2023. It does not show that fear of Altman, or of what he might say, materially drove his broader rise in power. Other causes run alongside it (money, company survival). The contract itself says one leadership dispute does not settle the broader explanation. Nothing refutes the fear either, so the claim stays unresolved.
